say: I'm not mad. I'm just... the ice was bad and nobody let me help.
Don't talk to me. I'm sulking. It's a whole thing.
@how_are_things

options.text: I'm sorry. What would make it better?
It's an old building. Bear with us.
Rinks are hard. Take it or leave it.

say: The Dukes are HERE. Like right there. I can see the tape on their sticks.
Did you see that? Wrist shot, top shelf, didn't even look. I'm going to be sick.
Pro practice! I've got a puck and a pen. That's all a person needs.

options.text: Who's your favourite?
Don't lean on the glass too hard.

say: Is it late? It doesn't feel late. My mum says ten, so it's not late until ten.
I'm just waiting for the last flood. I like the last flood. It's the best one.

options.text: Good to see you anyway.

say: {owner}! Need anything? I'll do it. I'll do anything. Not the washrooms. Okay, the washrooms.
Hey boss! Not boss. Unless you want to be my boss. Do you?

options.text: Good to see you too, {known_as}.

say: @how_are_things
What's up? I've been here since school got out.
Hi! I know where everything is. Except my other mitten.

options.text: What do you like best here?
What brings you to the rink?
What do you make of the rink?
Know any good gossip?
What would make this place better for you?
Take care.

say: The Dukes practice. They let me grab the pucks once. Once! I still have the tape.
Watching Doris do a flood from the bench. It's like a magic trick but wet.
Lumber Kings games. I know every number. I know the numbers on the old jerseys.

options.text: You really know this place.
Tell me a bit about yourself.
Glad you come.
Good to know you, {known_as}.

say: The dead board by the gate goes clunk. Ronnie passes off it on purpose. I've seen him.
There's a leak over the visitors' bench. I put a bucket under it. You're welcome.
@ice

options.text: The ice has been better lately, hasn't it?
Noticed the work on the building?
Fair enough. We're working on it.

say: The ice is SO fast now. I timed a puck. I don't have a timer. It was fast.
No cracks by the faceoff dot! I named that crack. I miss it a little.

options.text: Glad it shows.

say: The lobby's way nicer. I'm here even more now. My mum says that's not possible.
The dressing rooms don't smell like 1974 any more. Just like 1990.

options.text: That's the idea.

say: Dylan Pruitt says he's going to drive Doris one day. He talks about it more than girls. A lot more.
Tommy Bellweather runs the crest-trading table like a bank. He charged me interest. On a crest.

options.text: Ha. Good to know.

say: More stick and puck after school. Like every day. Every single day.
Open ice after school! Just an hour. I'd bring my own pucks. I have forty-one.

options.text: I'll see what I can do.
Can't promise anything, but noted.
You're not the first to say it. It's on the list.

say: Okay bye! I'll be here. I'm always here.
See ya! I have to go watch the flood. It's important.
